clue.text: Sailor's naughty love, free of responsibility

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; with the 's it gives AB'S

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters of love are put out of order

explanation.surface: A seaman's wayward romance, and him walking away from any responsibility for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' is the anagram signal on the four letters that follow it; AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to release them from blame or obligation, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary hydrogen, carbon and oxygen, all in a compound

definitions.text: Ordinary hydrogen, carbon and oxygen, all in a compound

indicators.note: a compound mixes its elements together, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson listing the elements that go into a compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a compound' mixes O, H, C, O and ALL. The whole clue also describes the answer: ethanol is a compound of just those three elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol, the drinkable kind, is a chemical compound made only of hydrogen, carbon and oxygen.

clue.text: Moving toward sea, this might make a splash.

indicators.note: moving shifts things about, so the letters of toward sea are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something heading for the sea, sure to land with a splash.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'splash' is a small dash of mixer added to whisky, not a splash in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash of fizzy mixer is a common addition to a whisky, so this carbonated drink could provide it.

clue.text: Unhurried movement getting stuck in vehicular go-slow

indicators.note: the answer is lodged inside the following words, stuck in them like a car in traffic

explanation.surface: A slow passage of time spent trapped in a traffic go-slow.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'movement' is a section of a piece of music, not motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a very slow tempo, so a slow section of a symphony carries that name.

clue.text: Horse just 2/3 length in lead, whinnying perhaps — it's uncertain

indicators.note: the trimmed horse is in the lead, coming in front of the next piece
only two thirds of the word is kept, so the six-letter word loses its last two letters

parts.note: an equine is a horse or other member of the horse family
whinnying is an example of making a sound with the voice

explanation.surface: A racehorse winning by two-thirds of a length, whinnying, with the result still in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just 2/3 length' trims EQUINE to EQUI; 'in lead' puts it ahead of VOCAL. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivocal means ambiguous or open to doubt, a direct synonym of uncertain.

clue.text: E.g. Benedictine rule spreads to include current queen

indicators.note: the rearranged rule takes in the next letters, including them inside
spreads suggests the letters of rule being spread out and rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A Benedictine monastery's rule being widened to cover the reigning queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Benedictine looks like a monk, but here it is the drink. 'spreads' scrambles the rule, and 'to include' sets the current and queen inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedictine is a herbal brandy-based drink originally made by monks, an example of a sweet after-dinner spirit.

clue.text: Succeeding learner is promoted in change

indicators.note: being promoted means moving up, so in this down entry the letter rises to the top

parts.note: to alter is to change
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A trainee gets promoted as part of a reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is promoted' moves the L of ALTER up to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming after something in time, as in a subsequent or following event, is the sense shared here.

clue.text: Crumbly new quiche's no good for slaking thirst

indicators.note: a crumbly quiche falls apart, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A crumbling, freshly made quiche is useless when you are thirsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbly' scrambles only new plus quiche; the abbreviation for no good is added unchanged at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake thirst is to satisfy it with a drink, which is exactly what putting out a thirst means.

clue.text: Begin in the middle of America originally going west

indicators.note: going west means dying or departing, and originally points to the first letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a middle is a centre, spelt the American way

explanation.surface: Starting a journey in the heart of the USA and heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of America' asks for the US spelling CENTER; 'originally going west' drops its first letter, C. 'go west' is slang for to perish.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter on something is to embark on it, so the verb can mean to start or begin.

clue.text: About to kidnap Hubble? This might be found in a bin

definitions.text: This might be found in a bin

indicators.note: kidnapping means holding someone captive, so the first piece takes the name inside it

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
Edwin Hubble was the American astronomer

explanation.surface: A plot to abduct the astronomer Hubble, and something lurking in the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bin' here is a wine bin, a rack for storing bottles, not a rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottles of claret and the like are stored in cellar racks called bins.

clue.text: Apple product got from dodgy credit mainly

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters are scrambled
mainly means most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An Apple gadget bought with dubious credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims CREDIT to CREDI and 'dodgy' rearranges it. Apple looks like the tech company, but it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented apple juice is a drink made from the fruit, so it is literally made from apples.

clue.text: Raw meat Mike left out turned bad

indicators.note: bad means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
left out means omitted, so that letter is removed from meat

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Uncooked meat left out by Mike has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' takes M from MEAT, leaving EAT; 'bad' shuffles EAT plus TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something raw is in its natural state, not processed or cooked.

clue.text: By all means hang around — so we got drunk

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to hover is to hang in the air

indicators.note: being drunk means staggering about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Permission to loiter, since the speakers ended up drunk anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got drunk' is the anagram signal, and 'around' makes hang wrap the scrambled pair; 'hang around' tempts as one phrase meaning loiter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in whatever manner, so by any method at all.

clue.text: Wow! A soldier — one attached to the queen?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Amazement at a soldier assigned to guard the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation like 'gosh'. The definition plays on Queen Elizabeth II's famous fondness for this breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II kept many Welsh dogs of this breed, so one was devoted to her.

clue.text: Toy company admits leader of tour for free

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the first piece takes in the letter

parts.note: Lego is the Danish maker of building bricks

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A toymaker offers a factory tour at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts T, from 'leader of tour', inside LEGO.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a grip on someone is to liberate them, so the verb phrase matches the verb free.

clue.text: Mineral drinks agenda surprisingly offering this?

definitions.text: Mineral drinks agenda surprisingly offering this?

indicators.note: drinks means swallows, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly arranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A meeting's agenda about soft drinks unexpectedly offering a fruity fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' makes ANGEAD from AGENDA, which ORE 'drinks'. In Britain 'minerals' are also fizzy soft drinks, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-flavoured fizzy drink is one of the soft drinks the British call minerals.

clue.text: Blend in on the way round motorway with the French

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the next piece is added on
the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: something coming is on its way
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Merging into traffic on a roundabout by a motorway, alongside some French drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' sets the motorway inside the phrase for on the way, and 'with' appends the French article. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle things together is to mix them, so the verb is a synonym for blend.

clue.text: It's refreshing seeing new summer month record for year

parts.note: in mint condition means brand new

indicators.note: one thing put for another is a substitution, so the record replaces the year

parts.note: July is a summer month in the northern hemisphere
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Refreshment found in a brand-new summer month's record of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals the record replacing the year in the month; mint condition means brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: This bourbon, sugar and mint cocktail served over crushed ice is a famously cooling drink.

clue.text: This syrup's sort of endearing

indicators.note: sort of hints at a loose version, so the letters of endearing are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A syrup whose sweetness is somewhat endearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ENDEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: This pomegranate-flavoured red syrup is used to colour and sweeten cocktails.

clue.text: Cover boy caught in onset of torrential rain storm

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the name goes inside the other letters
the onset of a word is its first letter
a storm whirls things about, so the letters of rain are rearranged

parts.note: Paul is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad caught out in a downpour that begins torrentially, needing shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' scrambles rain, 'onset of' takes the first letter of torrential, and 'caught in' puts the boy inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy waterproof sheet is used to cover things against rain, a noun synonym of a cover.

clue.text: Viruses of a kind to return around beginning of year

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the month
to return means to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sort is a kind
January, abbreviated Jan, is the start of the year

explanation.surface: A kind of virus that comes back around New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the kind, which goes 'around' the month. 'beginning of year' looks like a first-letter pick but is the month itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Trojan horses are malicious programs disguised as harmless software, loosely called computer viruses.

clue.text: Renewable sort of energy in the main?

indicators.note: sort of suggests a rough version, so the letters are rearranged
in the main means mostly, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether a clean, renewable energy source is mostly in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' trims ENERGY to ENERG, and 'sort of' rearranges it. 'Renewable sort of energy' tempts as one long definition; it splits after 'Renewable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewable power from wind or sun is described as environmentally friendly, the same eco sense of the colour word.

clue.text: Men with guts in a bad way and dribbles between legs

indicators.note: in a bad way means in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Men with sore stomachs, unwell and dribbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a bad way' rearranges MEN and GUTS. In British football slang, to nutmeg is to play the ball through an opponent's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Football slang names the trick of passing the ball between a defender's legs, a verb here in the third person.

clue.text: Outstanding argument right from the start

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the start of the word

parts.note: a row is an argument, and quarrelling is the -ing form, used here as a noun

explanation.surface: A brilliant argument, correct right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise but means unpaid. 'from the start' removes R from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding debt is one still unpaid, still due to be settled.

clue.text: Suffer by way of scoundrel

parts.note: in can mean by way of, as in paying in cash
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: Being harmed at the hands of a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a loss or penalty upon yourself is to undergo or sustain it.

clue.text: Old boy has two spurts in Duchamp's urinal, say?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a jet is a spurt of liquid, and a dart is a sudden rush; two spurts give both
a dart is a sudden rush forward, a second sense of spurt

explanation.surface: An old man producing two jets into Duchamp's famous urinal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two spurts' supplies two different synonyms of spurt in a row. Marcel Duchamp exhibited a urinal, 'Fountain', as art.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchamp's 'Fountain' is a readymade presented as a work of art, so it is an artistic object.

clue.text: Hack's run out all over newspaper

indicators.note: all over suggests turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a hack is a nag, a worn-out horse
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece has run out all across the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a reporter but is a horse. 'all over' reverses NAGRO. In cricket a batter can be 'run out'.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a publication speaking for a party or group, so a newspaper can be one.

clue.text: Pick-me-up is extremely pleasant but never finished

indicators.note: each word is never finished, so both lose their final letter

parts.note: too nice means extremely pleasant

explanation.surface: A restorative that is very pleasant, though nobody ever finishes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never finished' cuts the last letter from both TOO and NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative drink or medicine that perks you up, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Maybe Raphael's timeless art movement getting left behind

indicators.note: behind means at the back, so the letter comes last
timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: a change is a move or shift

explanation.surface: Raphael's timeless art movement being left behind by fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raphael' tempts as the painter; it is the angel. 'timeless' drops T from ART. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is one of the chief angels in Jewish and Christian tradition, an example of the rank.

clue.text: Innocent drinks company making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Evian is a French bottled water brand

explanation.surface: The smoothie maker Innocent Drinks returning to the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent' plus 'drinks company' looks like the British smoothie firm Innocent Drinks; the definition is just 'Innocent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naive means lacking worldly experience, which is what innocent means here.

clue.text: Society to encourage operator

parts.note: to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A group formed to motivate someone who runs machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator' looks like someone running a machine; it is one who operates in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who performs operations is someone who operates, hence one who works in a theatre.

clue.text: Pots on table? 6 of them will be needed

definitions.text: Pots on table? 6 of them will be needed

parts.words: Pots on table? 6 of them will be needed
parts.note: in snooker or pool, to pot a ball is to sink it, and a table has six holes for the balls to drop into

explanation.surface: Pots set out on a table, six of them required for the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pots' looks like cookware but is the snooker verb for sinking balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooker or pool table has six holes with bags, where potted balls end up.
